title: Human Capital-Driven Acquisition: Evidence from the Inevitable Disclosure Doctrine
eligible_reason: Staggered recognition of the Inevitable Disclosure Doctrine (IDD) by state courts (21 adopting states by 2013, three rejections: FL, MI, TX); binary treatment `idd` at the headquarters-state level; firm-year panel 1980-2013 (11,122 firms, 123,212 firm-years in the paper) with firm FE and Census-region x year FE, clustered by headquarters state. Table 3 column 1 has no controls and is eligible. Treatment switches off in the three rejection states (protocol: drop post-rejection periods where idd = 0).
design_notes: Linear probability model: Acquisition_{i,t} = a + b1 IDD_{s,t-1} + controls + Firm FE + Region x Year FE + e; IDD lagged one year (README: fyear is the year of the explanatory variables, dependent variable measured in t+1). Package MainSample.dta: 123,994 rows, 11,122 firms, fyear 1980-2013; idd = 1 in 55,853 rows; 5,958 firms ever treated, 5,164 never; 4,030 firms already treated at their first observed year (states recognizing IDD before 1980 or before firm entry); 879 firms' idd switches off (rejections in FL 2001, MI 2002, TX 2003 per literature); firm-level first-treatment years spread over 1980-2013 because of firm entry. Alternative variables: adoption (=1 from first recognition, stays on after rejection), rejection (=1 after reversal), adoption_m2 ... adoption_p3 event-time dummies. FE: firm + regionn##fyear (regionn = Census region of historical HQ state; four regions; time-invariant unless HQ moves). Cluster: hstate (historical HQ state).
estimators_reported: TWFE event study with controls (Table 3 col 5)

specs.code_line: reghdfe acquisition  idd  , absorb (firm regionn##fyear)  vce (cluster hstate)
specs.outcome_transform: binary indicator (firm acquired in year t+1), linear probability
specs.treatment_definition: IDD recognized in the firm's (historical) headquarters state in fiscal year t (lagged one year relative to outcome); binary; switches off after rejection in FL, MI, TX
specs.notes: R-squared 0.162. Intro headline '0.8 percentage point' matches all of columns 1-3 (0.008). Robustness tables build on column 3 (full controls). Protocol handling: drop post-rejection firm-years (idd switches off for 879 firms); 4,030 always-treated firms.

published_estimates.coef_source: PolyU accepted-manuscript PDF (ira.lib.polyu.edu.hk/10397/93051); table reports p-values, not SEs

screener_notes: Package: ~/did_packages/mnsc/mnsc.2020.3707/data/ with regression.do (Tables 2-3 only), MainSample.dta (analysis file, 123,994 rows; 123,212 used after missing controls), SAS data-construction code, ReadMe.pdf with variable list. Sources (SDC, Compustat, CRSP) are subscription-only but the analysis dataset is shipped. Only the baseline Table 3 is in the package; later tables (border matching Table 4, state-level Table 5, heterogeneity, retention, synergies, returns) are not replicable from the package and are mostly interaction/matching designs anyway. Eligible spec: Table 3 col 1 (idd, firm FE + region x year FE, cluster hstate). Handling notes for re-estimation: (i) idd switches off for 879 firms in FL/MI/TX after rejection -> drop post-rejection firm-years per protocol; (ii) 4,030 always-treated firms; (iii) regionn is based on historical HQ state and can change when a firm relocates (check within-firm variation); (iv) outcome is measured in t+1 relative to fyear. Published Table 3 reports p-values in parentheses (SE not printed).
